sections.text: Mentally renouncing all actions, the self-controlled soul enjoys bliss in this body, the city of the nine gates, neither doing anything himself nor causing anything to be done.
न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः।
The Lord of this universe has not ordained activity, or any incentive thereto, or any relation between an act and its consequences. All this is the work of Nature.
नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः।
The Lord does not accept responsibility for any mans sin or merit. Men are deluded because in them wisdom is submerged in ignorance.

So now we know that in my life, actions are necessary, but theyre also my assets. My actions are my assets. Well, Rajan, how did you accomplish what you accomplished? All that I have done -- went to architecture school, then worked for all these years for very little pay. My actions are my assets, but my actions are also a liability. So my actions are both the assets and the liabilities.
And what we try to do is leverage the assets and renounce the liabilities. When you file bankruptcy, what are you trying to do? Youre renouncing your liabilities. But at the same token, you have to renounce your assets as well. You know, a very good recent example -- HDL, a very well-respected, fastest-growing company, thousands of employees and millions of dollars of investment. They filed for bankruptcy. Not only their bad deeds and their debt they have renounced, but the assets also they had to renounce -- just got sold for like 32 or 37 million dollars.
There were probably hundreds of millions of dollars worth of investment. Bhagavan said that when you file bankruptcy on your liabilities, you have to also renounce your assets. So if I give up this sense of agency for both my good actions and bad actions, then Im free. No assets, no liability.
So Bhagavan said that one who takes the doership has to suffer through the merits or the sins of his actions. The Yogi, while working, realizes that he cant give up the agency, but he gives up the fruits of actions.
Whatever will come out, Ill accept. Because Im not the Karma-Phaladatta -- Im the actor. I have the capacity to act, empowered by the Lord as my consciousness. But I have no control over what comes out from the world. The world is the Karma-Phaladatta. When I practice architecture, all the efforts I put in -- I cant give myself a project.
Somebody else has to give me a project. So the Karma-Phaladatta is somebody other than myself. Now in our Puranic sense, we think that the Karma-Phaladatta is Bhagavan -- that Bhagavan is keeping score of what good deeds you have done, what bad deeds you have done. Therefore, when we go to the temple, what do we ask for? Bhagavan, maaf karna. Bhagavan, Bhagavan hoge.
We dont say, You remember what good deeds I have done -- Im in control, dont worry about it, Mr. Bhagavan. Just Bhagavan, maaf karna. So whenever we are in trouble, we ask Bhagavan to forgive us for all of our bad actions. But when it comes to success -- Im a self-made man. Came to this country with $8 in my pocket.
When I left India, the only thing I could take with me was $8. That was the total foreign exchange the Indian government allowed for people who leave India. So most of us came with $8 in our pocket. Your problems, Bhagavan -- you take care of it. But Bhagavan said, look, neither can I take care of your problems, nor can I give you credit for what you have done. Because all these actions which you are performing are in the realm of Prakriti.
Not in the realm of the self. Bhagavan is functioning in the realm of the self. So the verse which we will be seeing today says Nakartrutvam nakarmani lokasya srajati prabhuhu. This is completely in contrast to what we have believed all along -- that Bhagavan is the controller of all that I do. See, every time I make a mistake, I just say, what can I do?
Bhagavan has made me like that. Bhagavan put me in this situation. And thats a good comforting thought. That look, Im not doing anything wrong. Bhagawan is putting me in this situation. And also we have this Puranic idea that Chitragupta is writing this book.
When you die he will just open up your account and say look, what good deeds you did. What bad deeds you did. Well, looks like your balance is pretty good. Well, it looks like your account on the negative side so it will go to hell. So we thought that somebody is taking care of all these things. So we always have this comfort zone that Bhagavan is actively participating in my life and he is guiding me or he is maneuvering me to what I am doing.
But now this Verse says Bhagavan says, Im not doing anything. Nakartrutvam Nakarmani not the doership or the actions are created in this world by Prabhu. One who is a Prabha is a Prabhu. The Lord, one on which my life depends, is my Lord. The Lord is the one who sustains my livelihood. So my Lord is the one on whom my life depends.
So hes the Lord of my being, my consciousness. As long as Im alive, I am who I am. As soon as the consciousness leaves me, Im no longer who I am. That dead body -- you wont call it Rajan Bhat. You will get rid of it as quickly as you can. Because I am who I am because of the consciousness in me.
So here Bhagavan says, Nakaratrutvam Nakarmani -- nothing in this world is created by the Lord of your being, my consciousness. The self which I call myself, you call yourself, he calls himself, she calls herself -- it is not forcing you to do anything. Its not creating any actions for you. Its also not creating any sense of agency for you. Its not taking any part in anything which youre doing.
Then where does this idea of me doing things come from?
It comes from your identification with the conditioning of yourself. Navadvare puree dehi naiva kinchit karomi iti -- the verse says it is the embodied one in this nine gated city who thinks I am doing. The self says, I am not doing anything. But the one who identifies with this nine gated city becomes the doer. And that identifier is my ego that says this is me.
The ego is the doer because he is the identifier with the conditioning. So Bhagavan said, the self, I, the Lord of your being is not forcing you to do anything nor am I creating any actions for you. Hes also not the one who is actively sitting down with his supercomputer and saying Rajan did this. Hes completely out of this business. He simply says, let nature take care of it. Everything that is happening to me is happening because of the way I acted according to my nature -- the nature of my body, the nature of my mind, the nature of my intellect -- and then the nature of the world, what object I have acted upon, and at what level of physical abilities.
If I punch a guy who is 65 and about 300 pounds, what do you think the reaction would be? According to his Prakriti, according to my Prakriti -- Svabhavastu Pravartate. So Bhagavan said, in this world, actions are performed by the very nature of the beings -- the very nature of my body, mind, and intellect. And the Karma Phala coming to me is also dependent on the nature of the world. I always say, I may be the best architect on this planet, but if there is no work outside, no matter how much effort I put in, will there be any result?
Because the world is completely devoid of that need. But if I put my effort into a field where there is a need compatible with my ability, then I will get results. So what is happening? The Karma and Karma Phala are not dependent on whether Bhagavan thinks Im a good guy or a bad guy. Well, give Rajan some projects.
He takes Gita class on Sundays. My clients dont care whether I take Gita class or Bible class. They only care whether I can design their buildings effectively. So Svabhavastu Pravartate -- everything in this world is guided by the laws of nature. Bhagavan says, I as the Prabhu am not involved at all.
So please dont count on me. This is a big shocker for all of us. We always thought that no matter what bad I did, as long as I go to the temple, the coconuts I offer will take care of it. So Bhagavan said, I do not take part in any of that. Na Adatte Kasyachit Papam -- I do not take sins from anybody.
No matter what bad I do, Bhagavan says, it does not affect me at all. Na chaiva Sukritam Vibhuhu -- and also I dont accept any good deeds. Aap khud hi karaho, Bhagavan, you dont do anything for me. I dont accept anything.
I dont accept any of your good deeds or bad deeds. That self which is all-pervading is not affected by any good deeds or bad deeds in this universe. Myself, my consciousness, which I consider my Prabhu -- because I cannot sustain myself without him -- the same self is also Vibhu, all-pervading. So right now Im burdened by my sins.
In a sense Im burdened by what things I have done wrong in my life. I wish I had done this. I wish I had done this. I wish I had not put money in the market before it crashed. I wish I had bought Apple stock when it came out 25 years ago or whatever. But one said, but its not affecting me.
The self in me is not tainted by my sins, my bad deeds, or my good merits. So with all the good deeds and bad deeds happening in this world, we constantly ask this question: Why does Bhagavan let this happen? What is this ISIS doing? And tsunami, and all these terrorists, and all these things happening.
Is he sleeping at the wheel? He said, no, I really have nothing to do with it. Everything is happening as per the nature of the Prakriti. Once I have created the Prakriti, it is governed by its own laws. We know the laws -- Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas.
These laws, in their permutations and combinations, create this world of plurality. The world of plurality interacts with itself according to its own gunas and creates its own results. But I stay out of it. Once you create the laws of the game, the referee only judges the player based on the rules of the game -- not whether he thinks someone is a nice guy or a bad person. You have to play by the rules of the game.
Once I sit in my car and turn the ignition, the car does not know whether a nice person has turned the ignition or a bad person. It will go by how the laws of thermodynamics work in the engine. So Bhagavan says, I do not really accept any good deeds or bad deeds. Then why are we not seeing this? Why are we not seeing that all these things happening are very natural -- that they are happening exactly as they should? The world is perfect, as Dan used to say all the time.
The world as is is the way it should be. But I constantly think this world is not appropriate. I dont know why everything is so messed up. You know, its a chaos. But once I know its not a chaos, its the cosmos, its not a chaos. Things are exactly happening in your life as it should happen.
Because of what you did so far, things will happen in your future exactly as you build your future. But then I am completely confused about these laws of the game. Im actually participating in a game without knowing the rules of the game. Basically, thats the problem. If I start playing football without knowing what the rules are, Im going to be crushed. Thats exactly what is happening with me right now.
So Bhagawan says, why that is happening? Agnane Abrutam Gnanam this knowledge about the self is covered by the ignorance.

Verse 13 introduces the striking image of the body as a city of nine gates - the two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, mouth, and two lower openings. The self-controlled soul enjoys bliss dwelling within this city, neither doing anything himself nor causing anything to be done. Verses 14-15 deliver perhaps the most challenging teaching: the Lord does not create our sense of doership, does not ordain our actions, and does not accept responsibility for our sins or merits. All this is the work of Nature. Our confusion arises because wisdom is submerged in ignorance.
This teaching demands deep reflection. We habitually blame God when things go wrong and take credit when things go right. Today, examine this pattern in yourself. When you succeed, notice the thought I did this. When you fail, notice the tendency to blame circumstances, others, or even the Divine. Verse 14 states clearly: svabhavastu pravartate - it is your own nature, the interplay of body, mind, intellect with the world, that creates results. The Lord is like the sun - it enables all activity without participating in it, without preference for what grows in its light. Can you take full responsibility for your life while simultaneously releasing the ego that claims ownership? Sit with this paradox today: everything is happening according to natural law, yet you are not excused from the consequences of your actions. How does this understanding change your relationship with your choices?
